messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: stan syntax question
parts:
Hi, Bob. I programmed up Matt3's schools model as follows:

schools2.code <- '
data {
int[0,] J; // number of schools
real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
real[0,] sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}
parameters {
real mu;
real[0,] tau;
real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
real theta[J];
for (j in 1:J){
theta[j] <- mu + tau*eta[j];
}
}
model {
eta ~ normal(0,1);
for (j in 1:J)
y[j] ~ normal(mu + tau*eta[j], sigma[j]);
}
'

This worked fine. The only awkward parts were:

1. I needed to define y and theta componentwise; I couldn't get the vector assignments to work. It had a problem with "tau*eta", no matter how I did it, I couldn't get it to work.

2. I needed to repeat code (yuck!). I want to save theta, but if I define it as an intermediate quantity in the model, it won't be saved. So I needed to define it as a transformed parameter and then repeat the computation to save it there. Is that the only way to do this? I ask becasue I think it will be a fairly common occurrence that we will want to save something that we compute in the model stage.

See you
A

1. Maybe, but that's another hassle becasue then I have to change y and sigma to vectors too. No big deal perhaps but, in my mind, in that case y[j] would be a vector measurement (e.g., many observations on a single person) so that y would be an array of 8 vectors.
In general, the whole vector/matrix/array thing is confusing to me. But I am expecting that in more complicated problems it will become helpful to have these different ways of encoding an array.

2. No, that doesn't work (or, at least, it didn't work for me). I think the problem is that transformed parameters are computed at the end (conditional on the simulated parameters) whereas intermediate quantities are computed during the loop.

But maybe we could compute transformed parameters in the loop. For example, what about this:

We declare theta as a trandormed parameter ("real theta[J]").
Then we actually assign theta inside the loop.

That doesn't work now, but maybe it could be done???

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan syntax question
parts:
Here's a better way to express it in the version of Stan you have:

data {
int[0,] J;
real y[J];
real[0,] sigma[J];

}
parameters {
real mu;
real[0,] tau;

vector[J] eta;
}
transformed parameters {

vector[J] theta;
theta <- mu + eta * tau;
}
model {
for (j in 1:J) {

eta[j] ~ normal(0,1);
y[j] ~ normal(theta[j],sigma);
}
}

The redundancy goes away because you reuse the
transformed parameter in the model block.

Then the model can be expressed more concisely as:

model {
eta ~ normal(0,1);
y ~ normal(theta,sigma);
}

as soon as I add some new signatures to
stan/gm/function_signatures.hpp to let Stan know it
can handle the vectorization Daniel added on the C++
side to the normal distribution. You (Andrew)
won't see it on the R side until Jiqiang's next release.

I'm also beginning to see why we really want constrained
vectors -- this model would be clearer if sigma were declared
as a vector.

- Bob

Aaah, yes, it works now:

schools3.code <- '

data {
int[0,] J; // number of schools
real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
real[0,] sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}

parameters {
real mu;
real[0,] tau;

real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
real theta[J];
for (j in 1:J){

theta[j] <- mu + tau*eta[j];
}
}
model {
eta ~ normal(0,1);
for (j in 1:J)

y[j] ~ normal (theta[j], sigma[j]);
}
'

So users just have to remember to put transformed parameter assigmnents into the transformed block and parameter assignments in the model block.

This can be a little clunky but I can deal with it.
